previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia was admitted for substernal chest pain radiating to the left arm and back, triggered by a stressful argument with her son. The pain resolved with nitroglycerin and morphine. Evaluation showed no acute ischemic changes on EKG and normal cardiac enzymes, indicating no myocardial infarction. Her symptoms were consistent with prior stress-related episodes. She was hypoglycemic on arrival (glucose 43), which resolved, but her HbA1c was elevated at 10.0, reflecting poor long-term diabetes control. Triglycerides were markedly elevated, though not fasting. Social work addressed her concerns about verbal and physical abuse from her son; she elected to stay with her boyfriend and pursue a restraining order. She remained stable, with no recurrence of chest pain, and was discharged home with continued cardiac and diabetes medications and follow-up plans.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Other late effects of cerebrovascular disease, facial weakness

CORONARIES: The patient has a history of CAD. However, her 
cardiac enzymes were all negative during this hospitalization. 
She had no EKG changes or further episodes of chest pain. She 
was continued on Plavix. Her beta blocker was swiched to 
metoprolol tartrate when admitted. It was switched back to 
metoprolol succinate when she was discharged. She was also 
continued on aspirin. Her statin dose was increased. Given her 
negative recent stress, negative enzymes, and absence of 
symptoms, a decision was made not to undergo cardiac 
catheterization. She was given a new prescription for isosorbide 
mononitrate.

was necessary. Her dose of lisinopril was increased because of 
elevated blood pressure.

presentation. She was placed in her home dose of Lantus twice 
daily. She required additional sliding scale coverage. Her 
metformin was held in case she needed catherization. It was 
restarted upon discharge.
